{{Quote|Welcome to the Rimmer's Rest, best cantina in all of Nar ''Shaddaa''.|The bouncer's welcome|audio=NarShaddBouncer-WelcometotheRimmersRest.flac|<ref name="Dark Forces: Rebel Agent audio drama">[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
'''Rimmer's Rest''', also known as '''Smuggler's Bar''', was a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on the urbanized [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> A place for seedy people to hang out and do business, the cantina was well stocked with numerous drinks. [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] agent [[Kyle Katarn]] had a shoot-out with local mercenaries in the bar in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]].<ref name="DF2">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref>

==History==
Like many cantinas all around [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], it was a place for all kinds of creatures to hang out and do business, thanks both to its cosmopolitan character, and the tolerance of [[Weapon/Legends|weapons]] and their use;<ref name="RA">''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]''</ref> [[Timmy]] the bartender kept a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] underneath the bar table.<ref name="DF2" />. The cantina boasted a rich arsenal of all kinds of bottles, decanters, jars, bulbs, and inhalers, with 1,241 different intoxicants. It also provided sample cuisine from every corner of the galaxy.<ref name="RA" />

[[File:Smugglers_bar_booths.png|thumb|left|200px|8t88 in the bar]]
In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]] the bar was the meeting place between the [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] [[8t88/Legends|8t88]] and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. Expecting [[Agent/Legends|agent]] [[Kyle Katarn]], the droid wanted Fett to help extract from him information that he wanted; Fett, however, knew of Katarn's exploits on behalf of the Rebel Alliance and knowing that the man was extremely dangerous, declined 88's offer.<ref name="RA" /> However, 8t88 found less competent backup, including a [[Unidentified Gran (Rimmer's Rest)|Gran]] and a [[Unidentified bounty hunter (Rimmer's Rest)|second bounty hunter]].<ref name="RA" />

Indeed, Katarn showed up soon after, according to the droid's invitation, expecting information concerning [[Morgan Katarn|his father's]] [[Death/Legends|death]] holding his [[Bryar pistol/Legends|Bryar pistol]]. 8t88 revealed Jerec's responsibility for Morgan's death during the [[Subjugation of Sulon]], and his plans for the rebirth of the Empire.<ref name="DF2" /> While late to the confrontation, much to 8t88's annoyance,<ref name="RA" /> the hirelings moved in around Katarn, leveling their blasters at him and confiscating his. The Gran warned Katarn not to move and brought up the topic of having obtained a [[Hologram disc/Legends|holodisc]] from the [[Katarn family compound|home]] on the moon [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]], which belonged to Katarn's [[Parent/Legends|father]]. Unable to access the disc's contents due to its encryption, 8t88 attempted to force help from Katarn, which was the actual reason for luring him there. Katarn refused, and 8t88 departed, leaving his hirelings behind to kill Katarn.

Instead of immediately shooting Katarn, the Gran took the vacated seat across the table from him and asked the Rebel agent if he remembered him from their past encounter,<ref name="RA" /> giving Katarn the opportunity, in one swift move, to deftly throw the other thug over his shoulder, arm himself again<ref name="RA" /><ref name="Dark Forces: Rebel Agent audio drama" /> and slide out from the table.<ref name="RA" /> The Gran retrieved his [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]] and quickly exited the room,<ref name="DF2OSG">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref> but Katarn followed him to the main bar area<ref name="DF2" /> and shot him, as did a second Gran near the bar.<ref name="DF2OSG" /> Timmy demanded that he leave, and Katarn [[Mission to Nar Shaddaa (5 ABY)|ran after]] 8t88 and the stolen holodisc.<ref name="DF2" />

==Layout==
[[File:Rimmers_Rest_interior.png|thumb|right|200px|Interior of the cantina]]
Rimmer's Rest was situated in a larger building complex, with only one entrance via a sloping ramp, marked by a light-up snake creature (which looked like an [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Hieroglyphics|hieroglyphic]]<ref name="RA" />). The cantina proper consisted of two rooms and a small hallway that connected the two. The first room had a large open space and housed the bar. The second room had three booths, each with tables and chairs.<ref name="DF2" />

Other places of the establishment had more than a hundred booths that could accommodate both [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids and non-humanoids]], where they could make safe use of [[Stimulant/Legends|stimulant]] or depressant narcotics. To protect privacy (and hide the lack of hygiene) the ambient lighting was low; blinking white lights marked the aisles. Evenly spaced columns supported the ceiling, rippling with colored rings along their length; the ceiling was made of reflecting tiles.<ref name="RA" />

==Behind the scenes==
In [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II|''Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II'']], level 1: "The Double-Cross on Nar Shaddaa" is played in and outside of Rimmer's Rest. The name "Smuggler's Bar" was first mentioned in ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II: The Official Strategy Guide]]''.<ref name="StratGuide">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref> When the player enters the room with the bar, the bartender will grumpily tell Kyle to get out of his bar, because he always causes trouble.<ref name="DF2" />

Some events and descriptions in the cantina differ between the video game, the ''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]'' novelization and the [[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|audio dramatization]]; in the adaptations the bar is described much larger than what appears in the game. 8t88 finds Boba Fett in the booth in the novel, while in the dramatization Fett finds the droid first and announces his presence, saying that he prefers to arrange their business while standing. The subsequent skirmish with the thugs also differs between the game, the novel and the drama.
